One curve per species and stage: use against size, gradient and distance to a river, together

Source: R/tune_curve.R
knw_tune_curve.Rd

After knw_tune_score() has picked a rule, one GAM fits the rule's variables together on the scoring population: a tensor smooth of log size (the pick's size variable, width or MAD) and log distance downstream to the first river of the pick's exc_q m³/s, a smooth of gradient, and the same nuisance terms as the scorer (log_area, data set, era) with the watershed group as a random effect; binomial with a complementary log-log link, REML. The data-set and era coefficients carry the scorer's normal prior (prior_sd): where the two nearly coincide (steelhead's FDIS visits are its 1995-2004 visits) an unpenalised fit sends them to about +-30 with offsetting signs, and a held-out group that mixes the combinations takes one of those offsets. A distance the walk did not find (Inf) is censored at dist_cap_m, and distance enters as log(dist + 10). The model is one surface, never a product of one-variable curves, so a size effect that only holds far from a river is not counted twice.

Usage

knw_tune_curve(
  d,
  pick,
  walks,
  folds,
  resp = "U",
  cols = c(grad = "segment_gradient", width = "cw_deploy", mad = "mad_pick"),
  src = "pick",
  dist_cap_m = 50000,
  q_default = 10,
  k = c(size = 6, dist = 6, grad = 6),
  edge_stream = NULL,
  prior_sd = 2.5
)

Arguments

d

the scoring population, with resp, wsg, log_area, data_set, era, blue_line_key, downstream_route_measure and the columns cols name.

pick

one row of the scored grid: size_var, size_min, grad_max, exc_q, exc_d. With no exception, distance is to a river of q_default.

walks

the index knw_walk_index() returns.

folds

the named fold of each group, as knw_tune_score() returns it.

resp, cols, src

as in knw_rule_in().

dist_cap_m, q_default, k

numeric the spec's constants: the distance cap, the river size when the pick has no exception, and the basis sizes (size, dist, grad).

edge_stream

integer or NULL: the FWA edge types the visits in d were filtered on, recorded on the result as edge_stream so the grade's reference population can be taken from the curve (#72).

prior_sd

numeric(1) the standard deviation, on the cloglog scale, of a normal prior on the data_set and era coefficients, as in knw_tune_score(): a fixed penalty b^2 / prior_sd^2 per coefficient. Inf for none (the curve before #73's Phase 7).

Value

A list: model (the mgcv::gam), data (the rows fitted, with log_size, log_dist, grad), ref (the reference nuisance values a segment is predicted at: median log_area, modal data_set, latest era), dropped (visits with no size or gradient), capped (visits kept at the distance cap: no walk, or no river found), heldout (summed held-out deviance), edf (the smooths' effective degrees of freedom), and curves, a tibble of marginal curves (curve, x, rate, rel_rate, rel_lo, rel_hi, threshold) relative to the pick's thresholds, each other variable held at its reference; edge_stream, as given; dist_in_model, FALSE when the distances were too few to carry a smooth and size stood alone; prior_sd and cols, as given (cols[["grad"]] is the gradient the curve was fitted on, which a grade table records, #92).

Details

Its held-out deviance is reported on the scorer's own folds: the fixed terms are refit on the other folds, and each held-out group refits only its own intercept, as the grid's rules did, so the two numbers compare.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
s <- knw_tune_score(d, rule_in, grid, "U")
cv <- knw_tune_curve(d, s$rules[s$rules$recommended, ], knw_walk_index(walks), s$folds)
cv$heldout; cv$edf
} # }
